# Pinned JuiceFS SDK library source

This nested module is JuiceFS v1.3.1's complete `pkg/` library tree, its `cmd/` CLI tree and root `main.go`, `go.mod`, `go.sum`, and Apache-2.0 `LICENSE`, copied byte-for-byte from the module archive verified by the existing root `go.sum` (upstream tag v1.3.1, commit e0032b2ae5e9603403ca955eed7d05426f6f2f8c). It omits documentation, integration tests and SDK examples. The library replaces the SDK for this application; the CLI is built into the one JuiceFS executable the app ships. Existing copyright headers are retained.

The root module has a version-specific, repository-relative `replace` directive. Ordinary `go build` and `go test` use this source without environment flags, overlays, network forks, or edits to the shared module cache. Existing root dependency replacements remain in force.

The first upstream source change is `patches/0001-synchronize-upload-failure.patch`: `wSlice` uses an atomic cancellation flag instead of an unsynchronized error interface. The upload loop only needed a failed/not-failed signal; `Finish` still returns the original error. This fixes the read/write race exposed when one upload fails while sibling uploads continue. It does not join those workers, change retry limits, establish durability, or permit releasing process ownership early.

`SOURCE.json` records archive provenance, the verified module checksum, every upstream and local source hash, and the patch hash. From the repository root run `python3 scripts/verify-juicefs-sdk.py`; add `--archive /path/to/v1.3.1.zip` to independently verify the source against the complete upstream module ZIP. The root SDK acceptance test's corrupt-provider case exercises actual upload/Fsync failure under the race detector; keep that oracle when changing this patch.

`patches/0002-create-only-object-writes.patch` adds the optional `SupportCreateOnly` interface. S3 and MinIO send `If-None-Match: *`; HTTP 412 returns `os.ErrExist`, while conflicts and uncertain replies remain failures. Sharded storage forwards through its existing raw-key routing. File storage syncs the parent directory chain and a private file before publishing with a no-replace hard link, then syncs its parent; uncertain linked targets are retained. Configured directories must be trusted and stable. Existing ordinary `Put` behavior is unchanged. This adds four reviewed object-library source changes; it does not establish an operation manifest, exclude external writers/deletions, or qualify provider power-loss behavior.

`patches/0003-inode-bound-slice-allocation.patch` adds the optional `meta.InodeSliceAllocator` hook to the existing shared VFS writer. Allocation is serialized per slice before invoking a recording allocator; nonretryable registration errors do not expose an ID or retry forever. Metadata implementations without the interface retain ordinary `NewSlice` behavior. A controlled overlapping initial/Fsync test covers success and refusal. This hook does not stop background workers or grant publication/durability authority.

`patches/0004-preflight-link-counters.patch` validates each hard-link parent counter under WATCH before queuing namespace effects. Wrong-type, noncanonical, negative and overflowing counters are refused; same-parent increments are checked together, and the inode link count cannot wrap. A concurrent counter mutation aborts EXEC and is checked again. Actual Redis/SDK tests cover retained bytes, collisions, ordinary links and a held-EXEC mutation. This prevents the diagnosed counter failures from partially publishing a link; it does not provide rollback for other Redis runtime errors, resolve ambiguous EXEC replies, or authorize media receipts or local spool retirement.


The fourth patch also supplies optional `PublishNewName` and `RecoverNewName`
Redis methods. Publication guards a captured root-to-parent chain and exact
private stage identity, rejects an occupied target and configured quotas, and
updates public-link directory accounting in the same EXEC as namespace effects.
Recovery recognizes exact private/public tuples and repairs public parent totals
with a watched absolute write. Callers must fence previous processes and retain
immutable publication intent before using these methods. Ordinary Link behavior
is unchanged. This does not issue a durability receipt or retire local custody.

## Bundled executable and patch 0005

The app ships its own JuiceFS at `Contents/MacOS/juicefs`; the `jm5` CLI build places it beside `build/jm5`. `scripts/build-bundled-juicefs.sh` (used by `build-app.sh` and `build-cli.sh`) first runs `scripts/verify-juicefs-sdk.py`, then builds this module (`go build .` here, so upstream's own `go.mod`/`go.sum` choose the dependencies) with the tags and ldflags in `SOURCE.json` `binary`, and refuses a binary whose `--version` differs from `binary.version_output`. The runtime (`internal/juicefsbin`) resolves only that sibling executable and refuses any other configured path; it never searches PATH or Homebrew. `scripts/verify-build.sh` checks that the bundled juicefs exists, has the app's signer and reports the pinned version, and onboarding preflight checks the same.

`patches/0005-owner-keeps-kernel-mount.patch` makes the kernel mount belong to the process that started JuiceFS. Upstream v1.3.1 answers SIGTERM/SIGINT with `doUmount(mp, true)`, which on macOS runs `umount -f <path>`; the unmount stops new FUSE requests, then upstream flushes and closes the session. A path can name a newer, different mount by the time a signal is handled, so the patch keeps that ordering without the unmount:

- `installHandler` (`cmd/mount_unix.go`) hands SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP to `pkg/jmsignal`, which (1) stops the FUSE server with go-fuse `Server.Shutdown`, (2) runs `FlushAll`, (3) closes the session, releases object storage and exits 0 (1 if the flush failed). Requests that reach the kernel after step 1 wait there and are never acknowledged by this process; they fail when it exits. Stop is attempted once (patch 0008 changed this): go-fuse's own 10 s limit already bounds it, and if it fails (server not serving yet, or a request busy past 10 s, after which go-fuse resumes) the process flushes and closes its session anyway while the server still serves.
- The whole sequence has upstream's 30 s deadline. On expiry the process exits 2 without closing the session; Redis treats it like a crash and stale-session cleanup reclaims it later. Buffered data that did not reach object storage is lost from JuiceFS. JuiceMount runs without `--writeback` unless `JM_FUSE_WRITEBACK=1`, so nothing is staged locally; the spool keeps its safety copy because the drainer's close never returned. With `--writeback`, blocks already staged in `<cache-dir>/rawstaging` survive and the next mount uploads them, but a slice whose metadata commit did not happen is still not part of any file. Repeated signals during the sequence are logged and ignored, so a supervisor retrying SIGTERM cannot skip the flush; SIGKILL remains the owner's escalation. Neither exit code is `meta.UmountCode`.
- `doUmount` (`cmd/umount.go`) always returns a refusal, so the supervisor-restart, broken-mountpoint and `juicefs umount` paths cannot unmount either. JuiceMount runs JuiceFS in direct service mode (`JFS_SUPERVISOR` set, no `-d`), where none of those paths run.
- `pkg/fuse` no longer calls `fssrv.Unmount()` (a path `unmount(2)` on macOS) when `Serve` returns.

In the pinned `github.com/juicedata/go-fuse/v2` fork, `Server.Shutdown` does not unmount. It sets a shutdown flag so readers stop reading `/dev/macfuse`, wakes readers blocked in `read(2)` by running `df <mountpoint>` (a `statfs` read of the path; on a path that now names another mount it only fails to wake ours, and Shutdown then gives up), interrupts in-flight requests after 3 s, gives up after 10 s, and keeps the FUSE fd. While readers are blocked it starts a `df` about every 10 ms. The fork's only path unmount is `Server.Unmount` (`syscall.Unmount(dir, 0)` on darwin), which the patched binary never calls.

`pkg/jmsignal/jmsignal.go` is JuiceMount-owned source with no upstream counterpart; `SOURCE.json` records it under `local_files`.

## Patch 0006

`patches/0006-redact-redis-url-errors-default-ipv6-port.patch` records the SDK change made by commit a9f070c ("Preserve Redis connection settings across app clients"), which had edited the source without updating `SOURCE.json`. Redis metadata and Redis object-store URL parse errors no longer echo the URL (it can carry a password). In the metadata URL only (`pkg/meta/redis.go`), a bracketed IPv6 host without a port gets 6379 instead of go-redis treating the brackets as part of the host name; the object-store URL keeps upstream port handling. It stacks on patch 0004 for `pkg/meta/redis.go`. Patches apply in name order; `scripts/verify-juicefs-sdk.py --archive` applies them to the upstream ZIP and requires the result to equal this tree.

## Patch 0007

`patches/0007-jmdeny-erofs.patch` makes a write refused by JuiceMount's per-project Redis proxy (H-8 option B) reach the caller as `EROFS` ("Read-only file system") instead of `EIO`. The proxy answers a refused command or transaction with `-JMDENY <REASON> proj=<ino> holder=<principal>@<host> epoch=<n>`, after sending `DISCARD` upstream for a held `EXEC`, so nothing in that transaction committed. `errno` (`pkg/meta/utils.go`) maps an error starting with `JMDENY` to `EROFS` without the stack-trace log. `shouldRetry` (`pkg/meta/redis.go`) does not list the token, so the transaction is attempted once. In `pkg/vfs/writer.go`, a slice whose commit returns `EROFS` joins `ENOENT`/`ENOSPC`/`EDQUOT`: the error reaches `Flush`/`close` unchanged and the writer deletes the slice's uploaded blocks (`store.Remove`), because no metadata references that slice ID. In `pkg/meta/base.go` `compactChunk`, a compaction whose commit did not happen (`EINVAL`, which is how the Redis engine reports a refused compaction after its double-check, or `EROFS`) deletes its uploaded slice object directly with the `DeleteSlice` message when `--max-deletes 0` (the Mac mount; with deletes enabled `deleteSlice` removes it); upstream's `deleteSlice` does nothing at `--max-deletes 0`, so every refused compaction of a fragmented file in another Mac's project would leak up to 64 MiB. All three rely on the proxy invariant that JMDENY never follows a committed EXEC (documented at `errno`). juicefs has no hook to skip compaction for a project this Mac does not hold; compaction is triggered by reads (`baseMeta.Read`) and writes (`baseMeta.Write`) inside the meta engine. It stacks on patch 0003 for `writer.go`. Gates: `internal/bundledjuicefs` `TestH8BJMDENYIsEROFSSingleAttempt`, `TestH8BSliceCommitDenyCloseIsEROFS`, `TestH8BCompactionDenyLeavesNoUploadedSlice` and `TestH8BAuthRequiredMountFailsCleanly` (build tag `h8b_acceptance`, disposable Redis).

## Patch 0008

`patches/0008-stop-signal-never-remounts.patch` stops upstream's `launchMount` supervisor (`cmd/mount_unix.go`, used when `JFS_SUPERVISOR` is unset) from remounting a volume its owner stopped. The supervisor treated every child exit other than `meta.UmountCode` as a crash and restarted the mount 1 s later, so a SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP whose child exited 1 (flush failed) or 2 (`jmsignal` deadline) brought the volume back. The supervisor's signal goroutine now records that it forwarded a stop signal, and after `cmd.Wait` it returns the child's exit instead of restarting. `pkg/jmsignal` (local source) attempts Stop once; retrying a Stop that go-fuse already bounds at 10 s consumed the whole 30 s deadline before any flush. JuiceMount itself runs the service stage directly (`JFS_SUPERVISOR` set), so this supervisor path matters for a manual or CLI mount of the bundled binary.

## Gates

`internal/bundledjuicefs` gates patch 0005 from the root module: real-signal and fake-server ordering tests (no write acknowledged after the stop step), the deadline and repeated-signal test, an exact check of the effects `installHandler` wires, a source check of `doUmount`, a run of the SDK verifier, and a scan of every darwin/arm64 file in the binary's build for path unmounts (`Unmount`/`Umount` references including method values, exec of umount/diskutil/fusermount, `diskutil` strings).

`patches/0010-replacement-guards-and-cache-ownership.patch` records the guarded replacement checks in Redis and the resident-cache upload ownership changes. It stacks on the existing Redis and cached-store patches and adds the disk-cache delta. The replacement record, slice-graph helpers, Redis replacement helpers, and upload ownership tests are JuiceMount-owned files recorded under `local_files`. The archive verifier reconstructs the patched upstream files exactly; `build-app.sh` also checks the inventory before compilation.

`patches/0011-stage-birth-create-watch.patch` adds pre-MULTI WATCH coverage and fresh-create checks for exact reserved replacement stage names. It refuses unsupported ACL inheritance and prevents nonexclusive creation from adopting an existing stage. The local Redis birth helper grants no authority; atomic receipt issuance remains a disabled-by-default proxy capability until guarded upload recovery is qualified.

`patches/0012-born-stage-upload-watch.patch` prepares guarded writes and timestamp updates for born stages. It WATCHes reciprocal custody, publication, namespace and current authority keys before mutation, rejects prepared stages and preserves mode and identity. Committed files resume ordinary lease-governed operations. Prefixed Redis Cluster volumes skip this unprefixed protocol, which does not support birth creation there.
